title: Active & Passive Voice — Imperatives, Modals & Prepositional Verbs
description: Imperative sentences (commands, requests, advice, prohibitions), modal auxiliaries (simple aur modal-perfect), prepositional aur phrasal verbs mein fixed prepositions ka retention, aur two-object passive constructions ko master karein.
learningObjectives: Imperative sentences ko unke communicative function (orders, requests, instructions, advice, prohibitions) ke hisaab se natural passive constructions mein convert karein
Textbook imperative pattern 'Let + object + be + V3' aur situational passive forms ('You are requested / ordered / advised to') ke beech accurate distinction karein
Negative imperatives aur prohibitions ke passive structures ('Let + object + not + be + V3' aur 'You are forbidden / instructed not to') ko master karein
Moral obligation aur advice wale sentences mein 'should be + V3' aur 'must be + V3' passive patterns apply karein
Modal auxiliaries (can, could, may, might, must, should, would) ke standard passive structure 'modal + be + V3' ko accurately transform karein
Modal-perfect passive structure 'modal + have been + V3' ko past unfulfilled actions aur deductions ke context mein master karein
Negative aur interrogative modal passives mein correct auxiliary chain aur inverted word order preserve karein
Prepositional aur phrasal verbs (look into, laugh at, deal with, call off) mein required prepositions ko passive voice mein retain karein
Direct aur indirect objects (two-object verbs) wale active sentences se dono alternative passive forms construct aur evaluate karein
High Court competitive exams ke advanced voice traps (missing prepositions, modal backshifting, incorrect negative order, been omission) ko eliminate karein

included: Imperatives with objects: 'Let + object + be + V3' pattern
Imperatives expressing requests: 'You are requested to + V1' pattern
Imperatives expressing orders/instructions: 'You are ordered/instructed to + V1' pattern
Imperatives expressing advice or moral duty: 'Subject + should/must + be + V3' pattern
Negative imperatives and prohibitions: 'Let + object + not + be + V3' aur 'You are forbidden to / instructed not to'
Simple modal passives: 'Modal + be + V3' across can, could, may, might, must, should, will, would, ought to
Modal perfect passives: 'Modal + have been + V3' for past unfulfilled actions or deductions
Negative and interrogative modal passive constructions
Preposition retention rule: retaining essential prepositions in prepositional verbs (looked into, laughed at, dealt with)
Multi-word and phrasal-prepositional verbs in passive constructions
Two-object active sentences: indirect object promotion vs direct object promotion with 'to/for'
excluded: Direct & Indirect Narration reporting rules, backshift tables, and pronoun shifts (covered in Lessons 06 & 07)
Sentence transformations regarding polarity and degree of comparison (covered in Lessons 08 & 09)
Subject-Verb Concord non-voice rules (covered in Lesson 13)
